concerns.text: FR-002 mandates extraction of 'reported values' but lacks a verifiable procedure to distinguish 'reported' from 'imputed' values when a PDF contains ambiguous text (e.g., 'approx. 50%'). The requirement states 'MUST NOT impute' but provides no deterministic rule or regex pattern to handle non-numeric or range-based reporting, making the 'no imputation' constraint untestable by an automated script.

FR-006 requires a 'Kruskal-Wallis H test' on 'raw extracted metric values' but the schema in 'Key Entities' only defines 'raw_value' as a single numeric field. It does not specify if 'raw_value' represents a single study's aggregate or a list of per-client metrics. Without a defined data structure (e.g., 'list of floats' vs 'single float'), the testability of the '≥3 raw data points per group' condition is ambiguous.

SC-002 defines a pass criterion of '0 errors in 5 randomly selected rows'. This is not statistically measurable for a deterministic pass/fail of the *system* because a single error in the 6th row would pass this test. The criterion measures a sample, not the system's total accuracy. A measurable SC must define the *tolerance* for the whole dataset (e.g., 'error rate < 1% across all rows') or define the sample size as the *entire* dataset if N < 100.

SC-005 requires a validation script to confirm 'every numerical value... matches a value present in extracted_metrics.csv'. This is untestable as written because the spec does not define how to handle mathematical transformations (e.g., 'mean of 3 values' or 'log-transformed value'). The script cannot verify a 'direct mathematical transformation' without a defined set of allowed operations or a traceability map linking report cells to specific CSV rows and formulas.
